study_design: Outpatient clinic-based case-control study of recently diagnosed, histologically confirmed prostate cancer cases and histologically confirmed controls.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: An outpatient clinic-based study of 89 cases and 38 controls was conducted in North Carolina between July 1989 and December 1991.
reason: The study evaluates prostate cancer generally and does not report an aggressive, advanced, metastatic, high-grade, high-risk, or lethal endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Linoleic acid consumption was positively associated with prostate cancer risk.
estimate_classifications.reason: The linoleic acid estimate concerns prostate cancer overall, with no aggressive disease restriction.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Our data failed to demonstrate consistently a protective effect of marine omega-3 fatty acids on prostate cancer.
estimate_classifications.reason: The omega-3 finding concerns prostate cancer overall. The abstract supplies no effect estimate with both confidence bounds for this exposure.
